jobs.occupation: We Are Hiring – Experienced Chef
jobs.description:
EU/EEA citizenship or valid right to work in Denmark required

Ærø Hotel is looking for an experienced, skilled and reliable Chef to join our international kitchen team.

We are located on the beautiful Danish island of Ærø, in the maritime town of Marstal. We are looking for an experienced chef who enjoys working in a structured professional kitchen, preparing good-quality food for a large number of hotel guests.

We have 1 position available.

About the position

You will become part of our evening kitchen team, which consists of five chefs working closely together.

Ærø Hotel does not operate an à la carte restaurant.

Our kitchen is based on planned production and pre-arranged menus for our hotel guests. We serve between approximately 100 and 200 guests every day.

During the day, we prepare and serve lunches, while dinner consists of pre-booked and predetermined two-course menus.

Our dinner concept follows a fixed rotation of four different two-course menus. After the fourth menu, the rotation starts again on day five.

This means that our kitchen operation is highly structured, allowing the team to focus on good preparation, consistency, quality and efficient service.

We are therefore looking for an experienced chef who is comfortable preparing food in larger quantities and who understands the importance of planning, organisation and consistency when serving many guests.

The primary working language in our kitchen is Spanish, while English is the common language throughout the rest of the hotel.

Your main responsibilities

• 
Preparing lunches and evening meals for our hotel guests

• 
Preparing and cooking food for approximately 100–200 guests per day

• 
Working with our fixed rotation of pre-planned two-course dinner menus

• 
Taking responsibility for your own tasks and preparation

• 
Working closely with our team of five evening chefs

• 
Ensuring consistent quality, taste and presentation

• 
Planning and organising preparation efficiently

• 
Contributing to a smooth and well-organised dinner service

• 
Maintaining high standards of cleanliness and hygiene

• 
Following Danish food safety and hygiene regulations

• 
Supporting your colleagues and contributing to a professional and positive working environment

We are looking for someone who

• 
Has solid professional experience working as a chef

• 
Is experienced in preparing food for larger groups of guests

• 
Is comfortable with high-volume food production

• 
Is able to work independently and take responsibility

• 
Understands the importance of planning, preparation and consistency

• 
Works efficiently and remains organised during busy periods

• 
Speaks Spanish and is able to communicate in English

• 
Is reliable, responsible and flexible

• 
Takes pride in food quality and presentation

• 
Enjoys working as part of a professional kitchen team

• 
Has EU/EEA citizenship or another valid right to work in Denmark

Previous professional experience as a chef is essential for this position.

Salary and employment conditions

Salary: DKK 180 per hour before tax.

Holiday allowance is paid in addition to the hourly salary in accordance with Danish regulations.

We offer attractive working hours and the opportunity to become part of an established and experienced kitchen team.

Start date: As soon as possible

Location: Ærø Hotel, Marstal, Denmark

Staff accommodation

If needed, we can offer staff accommodation close to the hotel.

The current accommodation consists of private bedrooms with shared kitchen and bathroom facilities.

Rent is DKK 750 per week and includes:

• 
Electricity

• 
Water

• 
Heating

• 
Internet

During the coming winter, the staff accommodation will undergo a complete renovation. After the renovation, each room will have its own private bathroom and small kitchen.

Accommodation is optional and paid by the employee.

About Ærø Hotel

Ærø Hotel is a well-established hotel located in Marstal on the island of Ærø in southern Denmark.

We welcome guests from Denmark and abroad and have an international team of employees from several different countries.

Our kitchen is an important part of the hotel experience. Because most of our guests stay with us as part of organised hotel packages, we know in advance how many guests we are cooking for and which menus will be served.

This gives us a structured way of working, where good preparation, teamwork and consistency are essential.

You will become part of an experienced kitchen team where everyone works together to ensure that between 100 and 200 guests receive a good dining experience every day.

Life on Ærø

Ærø is one of Denmark’s most beautiful and distinctive islands.

The island is known for its beautiful coastline, beaches, historic towns, colourful houses, maritime atmosphere and relaxed way of life.

Marstal has a strong maritime tradition and is a lively small town with shops, cafés and the everyday facilities needed when living on the island. At the same time, the sea and nature are always close by.

Working at Ærø Hotel gives you the opportunity to combine a professional job with life in a safe, peaceful and welcoming island community.

For the right person, Ærø offers much more than just a workplace. It is an opportunity to become part of an international team while experiencing a very special part of Denmark.

If you are an experienced chef and would like to become part of our team at Ærø Hotel, we would be very pleased to hear from you.

Please send us your CV together with a short introduction about yourself, your professional kitchen experience and when you would be available to start.

jobs.occupation: Postdoctoral Position in Multiphysics Modelling of Bubble Transport and Electrochemical Processes in Alkaline Electrolysers
jobs.description:
The Centre for Industrial Mechanics in Sønderborg, Denmark, part of the Institute of Mechanical and Electrical Engineering, University of Southern Denmark (SDU), invites applications for a 2-year postdoc position in Multiphysics Modelling of Bubble Transport and Electrochemical Processes in Alkaline Electrolysers. The position is open from October 1, 2026, or as soon as possible thereafter, and the specific start date will be agreed with the successful candidates.

 

About the Position

The position is funded through a collaborative research and innovation project involving SDU, DTU, and Stiesdal Hydrogen, and aims to reduce the CAPEX of green hydrogen production by developing a next-generation bipolar electrode cassette for alkaline electrolysers. One focus will be on geometry-driven bubble management.

As a postdoctoral researcher, you will join the SDU Energy Systems Group at the Centre for Industrial Mechanics (CIM) and play a key role in developing advanced simulation tools and validating simulations with experimental results. Your work will combine multiphase CFD modelling, current distribution modelling, and collaboration with experimentalists. The objective is to create predictive models that guide cassette design, identify optimal operating conditions, and reduce the need for extensive physical prototyping.

Working closely with researchers at SDU and DTU, as well as engineers at Stiesdal Hydrogen, you will contribute to the development of next-generation hydrogen production technology with clear industrial impact and support its path towards large-scale implementation.

 

Your Role

• 
Develop and apply simulation methods for multiphase transport and current distribution 

in electrolyzers

• 
Investigate bubble-buoyancy-driven internal electrolyte circulation

• 
Quantify transport processes affecting mass transfer and electrochemical performance

• 
Integrate computational and experimental results to advance mechanistic understanding and predictive modelling

• 
Collaborate with academic and industrial partners

• 
Mentor and supervise students (PhD, MSc, BSc) on related research questions

• 
Publish research results in peer-reviewed journals and present at international conferences

• 
Contribute to research funding applications and assist with teaching activities as relevant

 

Your Profile

• 
PhD in engineering, computational science, physics or related discipline

• 
Background in computational fluid dynamics (CFD)

• 
Experience in multiphase flow and/or electrochemical transport modelling

• 
Experience with numerical simulation software such as ANSYS, COMSOL, or OpenFOAM 

• 
Programming skills in Python, C++, or equivalent languages

• 
Strong teamwork, communication, and independent research skills

• 
Proficient in English (spoken and written)

 

Why Join SDU Sønderborg?

The SDU Energy Systems Group at CIM is a dynamic, recently established research group within the Institute of Mechanical and Electrical Engineering (IME). As part of a young and growing team and institute, you will help shaping research, education, and innovation in engineering science. 

You will have access to state-of-the-art computing and lab facilities, and benefit from strong academic and industrial networks across Denmark and Europe. CIM is based at SDU’s scenic Sønderborg campus in the Alsion building directly at the waterfront. All study programs are taught in English, and more than half of our students and staff are international, creating an inspiring environment.

SDU maintains close ties to industry in Sønderborg, Southern Denmark, and Northern Germany, offering direct exposure to real-world challenges and opportunities for cross-sectoral research collaborations. This position offers you the chance to develop your own research ideas, contribute to the growth of the group and institute, and advance your career in a supportive, international setting.

In short, you will benefit from:

• 
Access to state-of-the-art computing and lab facilities

• 
A dynamic, international research environment in a scenic campus setting

• 
Close ties to industry and opportunities for cross-sectoral collaboration

• 
Support for developing your own research ideas and career

 

Contact information

For further information, please contact Associate Professor Martin Lautenschläger 
(mlaut@sdu.dk; phone: + 45 65 50 79 86) or Associate Professor Lars Duggen (duggen@sdu.dk) and visit www.sdu.dk/en/ime.

If you experience technical problems, please contact our email support.

 

Application

Applicants are advised to read the SDU information on how to apply.

Assessment of the candidates is based on the application material, and the application must include: 

• 
Motivated application.

• 
Curriculum Vitae. 

• 
Master’s and PhD degree certificates or equivalent (original and an official English translation).  

• 
Complete list of publications.

• 
Publications most relevant to the position.

• 
Summary and documentation of experience in teaching, if relevant to the position. 

• 
A research statement may be included.

• 
References/reference letters may also be included.

• 
A statement/documentation of other qualifications relevant to the position may also be included.

All documents must be in English and PDF format. CPR number (civil registration number) must be crossed out. All PDF-files must be unlocked, allow binding and may not be password protected. 

SUBMISSION GUIDE: Motivated application must be uploaded under ‘Cover letter’ (max. 5 MB), Curriculum Vitae must be uploaded under ‘Resume’ (max 5 MB). All other documents must be uploaded under ‘Miscellaneous documents’ (max 10 files with a maximum 50 MB per file). 

 

The application deadline is September 15, 2026, at 11:59 PM/23:59 (CET/CEST) 

 

Assessment and selection process

Applications will be assessed by an expert or assessment committee. Shortlisting may be applied, and only shortlisted candidates will receive a written assessment. Read about shortlisting at SDU.  Interviews and tests may be part of the overall evaluation.

Read about the Assessment and selection process.  

 

Employment terms

Appointment as a postdoc is temporary for an initial 2-year period, and the preferred start date is from October 2026. The start date may be adjusted to comply with processing times for any work- and residence permits.  Extension may be possible depending on available funding.

Employment as a postdoc requires academic qualifications at PhD level at the time of employment. Employment will be in accordance with the collective agreement between the Ministry of Finance and the Danish Confederation of Professional Associations for academics in the state including the associated circular on the protocol for the job structure for academic staff at Danish universities and the provisions for postdoc as described therein. 

Salary is determined in accordance with the applicable collective agreement and based on objective and gender-neutral criteria, including the content of the position, responsibilities, and qualification requirements. As an applicant, you are entitled to information about the starting salary and salary range for the position. This information will be provided during the recruitment process. SDU does not collect information on applicants’ previous salary. Further information on salary and taxation. 

Persons employed in the position may, based on a specific individual managerial assessment, be exempted from time registration, also known as a “self-organizer”.

-

The University of Southern Denmark wishes its staff to reflect the surrounding community and therefore encourages everyone, regardless of personal background, to apply for the position. SDU conducts research in critical technologies, which, due to the risk of unwanted knowledge transfer, is subject to a number of security measures. Therefore, based on information from open sources, background checks may be conducted on candidates for the position(s).

Further information for international applicants about entering and working in Denmark. You may also visit WorkinDenmark for additional information.

Further information about The Faculty of Engineering.

jobs.occupation: PhD Position in High Performance Organic Photovoltaics
jobs.description:
The Centre for Advanced Photovoltaics and Thin-Film Energy Devices (SDU CAPE), Mads Clausen Institute, University of Southern Denmark (SDU), invites applications for a 3-year PhD position within the DFF funded project LuminOPV. The position is open from Dec. 1, 2026, and the specific start date will be agreed with the successful candidates. 

 

What we offer 

The PhD position is a part of the SDU CAPE research center at the Mads Clausen Institute, SDU, where we focus on designing, developing, and bringing forward new sustainable solar energy conversion and storage technologies, in particular new thin film solar cells and modules. The DFF LuminOPV project will explore aggregation-induced emission (AIE)-active molecular materials to control photophysical processes, molecular organization, and energy losses in organic photovoltaics. Complementary interface engineering and passivation strategies will be employed to optimize charge extraction, suppress interfacial defects, enhance operational stability, and facilitate scalable organic solar cells and modules. 

This PhD project focuses specifically on the design and development of AIE-active molecular materials for next-generation organic photovoltaics. The project will be part of the DFF1 project, and research stays abroad is part of the position. Most of your working time is devoted to your own research studies. As a PhD student you are expected to develop your own ideas and communicate scientific results in English. We offer a fully funded PhD position for the duration of three years. 

The successful applicant will be enrolled as a PhD student at the PhD School at the Faculty of Engineering.

 

What we expect 

Candidates who hold a master’s degree in a relevant field (chemistry, material science, physics, electrical engineering and similar). Preferred candidates have experience with some of the following: Organic synthesis, molecular photophysics, organic and/or hybrid semiconductors, thin films and interfaces, and organic photovoltaics. Due to the high cross-disciplinary nature of the work, the candidate is expected to have excellent collaboration skills. A very good capability of communicating scientific results in English, both orally and in writing is required.

 

Workplace description 

We are an international research center working in the field of green energy technologies (CAPE), and we are looking for a highly motivated PhD candidate to join our CAPE research center at University of Southern Denmark (SDU), campus Sønderborg, for developing next-generation sustainable and high-performance photovoltaics. We offer a modern, inclusive, international and interdisciplinary working environment with state-of-the-art facilities as well as a strong tradition of international collaboration. Our ambition is, to recruit, develop, and retain talented scholars committed to both academic excellence and departmental development.

Having a focus on green energy technologies - improving performance, device stability and up-scaling, the center has full access to an ISOS5 cleanroom and surface science laboratory facility for the preparation and characterization of thin films and photovoltaic devices, as well as a fully equipped Roll-to-Roll (R2R) facility for upscaling flexible devices. Our research center CAPE is a partner in various national and international research projects and networks that include collaboration partners from both academia and industry. 

 

Further information 

For information about the CAPE research center, please see https://www.sdu.dk/en/forskning/cape 

For information about the Mads Clausen Institute, please see www.sdu.dk/en/mci

Further information about this position is available from Associate Professor Vida Engmann, e-mail: engmann@mci.sdu.dk.

If you experience technical problems, please contact our email support.

 

Application

Before applying the candidates are advised to read the Faculty information for prospective PhD students and the SDU information on how to apply.

Assessment of candidates is based on the application material, and the application must include: 

• 
Motivated application. 

• 
Curriculum Vitae.

• 
Master’s and Bachelor’s degree certificates or equivalent, including transcripts of grades (original and an official English translation). 

• 
Completed TEK PhD application form for 5+3 applicants. Find the form at the Faculty website.

• 
Completed TEK PhD form for calculation grade point average. Find the form at the Faculty website. 

•

• 
Only for applicants from programmes that evaluate thesis/examination project by approved/not approved: An official written assessment of the thesis or dissertation project from the grade giving institution. The statement must clearly state that the candidate has been among the top 30 pct. in the graduation class for the study programme.

• 
List of publications and maximum 2 examples of relevant publications (in case you have any publications).

• 
References may be included, you're welcome to use the form for reference letter at the Faculty website.

• 
A statement/documentation of other qualifications relevant to the position may also be included.

All documents must be in English and PDF format. CPR number (civil registration number) must be crossed out. All PDF-files must be unlocked, allow binding and may not be password protected. 

SUBMISSION GUIDE: Motivated application must be uploaded under ‘Cover letter’ (max. 5 MB), Curriculum Vitae must be uploaded under ‘Resume’ (max 5 MB). All other documents must be uploaded under ‘Miscellaneous documents’ (max 10 files with a maximum 50 MB per file). 

 

The application deadline is October 15, 2026, at 11:59 PM/23:59 (CET/CEST)

Enrollment and employment terms

Appointment as a PhD fellow is a 3-year salaried position, and the monthly gross salary incl. pension is 37.075 DKK. If you have relevant postgraduate experience, you may be placed on a higher salary step. 

Applicants must hold a master’s degree (equivalent to a Danish master's degree) at the time of enrollment and employment. Employment is contingent on enrollment approved by the PhD School. jobs.occupation: Postdoc in Microbiome Bioinformatics Workflows
jobs.description:
A position as a postdoc (100% time) is vacant at the the Arumugam Group, Research unit of Medical Gastroenterology, the Department of Clinical Research, Faculty of Health Sciences, University of Southern Denmark. 

The position is limited to 3 years with the possibility of extension. 

Research tasks 

The position as a postdoc consists of research, teaching, professional development, and guidance in Microbiome Bioinformatics Workflows

We seek a bioinformatician to develop computational workflows to analyze large-scale microbiome multi-omics data in multiple projects studying human and animal health, including the consortium project PIG-PARADIGM to combat antimicrobial resistance (AMR) in pig production (http://pig-paradigm.net) and EU Horizon 2020 project MICROB-PREDICT (https://microb-predict.eu/). We strive to implement efficient and scalable workflows to analyze and integrate these data derived from metagenomics, metatranscriptomics, viral metagenomics, metabolomics, and metaproteomics in collaboration with international data science partners (e.g., EMBL-Heidelberg; University of California, Davis) and other project partners. We have developed the MIntO package (https://github.com/arumugamlab/MIntO) that integrates microbiome metagenomic and metatranscriptomic data. Our ambition is to develop new workflows that expand MIntO’s features (e.g., novel analysis types) as well as datatypes (e.g., metabolomic data).

In this position, you will be:

•

jobs.description:
A position as a postdoc (100% time) is vacant at the Arumugam Group, Research unit of Medical Gastroenterology, the Department of Clinical Research, Faculty of Health Sciences, University of Southern Denmark. 

The position is limited to 3 years with the possibility of extension. 

Research tasks 

The position as a postdoc consists of research, teaching, professional development, and guidance in Host-Microbiome Multi-omic Data Science.

We seek a data scientist to derive insights from host-microbiome multi-omics data in multiple consortium projects studying human and animal health, including GALAXY/MicrobLiver studying liver fibrosis (https://www.sdu.dk/en/forskning/galaxy), MICROB-PREDICT studying late-stage liver cirrhosis (https://microb-predict.eu/), and PIG-PARADIGM to combat antimicrobial resistance (AMR) in pig production (http://pig-paradigm.net). We strive to integrate and interpret these data derived from microbiome (e.g., metagenomics, metatranscriptomics, viral metagenomics, metabolomics, metaproteomics) and host (e.g., genetics, proteomics, circulating metabolomics) in collaboration with international data science partners (e.g., EMBL-Heidelberg; University of California, Davis) and other project partners. The current state-of-the-art for multi-omics integration and interpretation leaves much to be desired. Fortunately, our ongoing work leveraging a deep learning approach (autoencoders) integrates multi-omics data and generates biologically relevant insights using a biologically informed machine learning framework. Our ambition is to strengthen and expand this research direction into graph-based approaches such as graph neural networks.

In this position, you will be:

• 
Responsible for improving and expanding our current deep learning approaches, while also having a chance to create your own novel approaches.

jobs.occupation: Critical Environment Technician
jobs.description:
Overview
Critical Environment Technician (CET) – Shift Role 
Location: 3 Sites Greater Copenhagen Area, Denmark  
Role Type: Shift-based, onsite technical operations role 

Role Summary Microsoft is seeking a Critical Environment Technician (CET) to support the safe, reliable, and efficient operation of Microsoft datacenter infrastructure in Denmark. 
This role is responsible for supporting the operation, monitoring, maintenance, and troubleshooting of electrical, mechanical, cooling, and control systems within a 24/7 mission-critical environment. 

We offer an excellent work-life balance 
•    Two-day shifts from 6:00 AM to 6:00 PM. •    Two-night shifts from 6:00 PM to 6:00 AM. 
•    Seven days off following each rotation, in accordance with the DI agreement. 
Microsoft Culture and Expectations 
Microsoft’s mission is to empower every person and every organization on the planet to achieve more. Within CO+I, this mission is supported through a culture focused on safety, reliability, sustainability, inclusion, learning, and continuous improvement. 
Employees are expected to model Microsoft values, follow approved procedures, apply STOP WORK authority when needed, and contribute to an inclusive environment where all team members can perform, grow, and succeed. 

Responsibilities
Key Responsibilities 
•    Monitor, operate, and control critical infrastructure systems, including electrical, mechanical, cooling, and control systems. 
•    Perform preventive and corrective maintenance in accordance with approved EOPs, MOPs, and SOPs. 
•    Respond to incidents, support troubleshooting and recovery activities, and lead response efforts when appropriate. •    Identify and escalate safety, compliance, and operational risks in line with Microsoft standards. 
•    Collaborate with internal teams, vendors, and cross-functional stakeholders to ensure safe and high-quality execution. 
•    Contribute to continuous improvement by sharing knowledge, supporting peers, and developing technical capability over time. 

Qualifications
Required Qualifications 
 •    Upper secondary education (vocational or general upper secondary school) or equivalent practical work experience 
•    Some prior experience in technical work, such as: industrial maintenance, electrical or HVAC installations, energy, process or production facilities, datacentres, hospitals or other demanding technical environments 
•    You will be required to travel between sites as part of this role so a valid driver’s license will be required.
•    Ability to work rotating shift patterns in a 24/7 operational environment. 
•    Ability to communicate effectively in English. 
Preferred (but not essential) Qualifications 
•    Technical certification in electrical, mechanical, HVAC, or a related field, or equivalent training. 
•    Experience working with CMMS systems. •    Experience in high-availability, mission-critical, or safety-critical environments. 
•    Exposure to industrial, electrical, mechanical, cooling, or control systems.  

Direct datacenter experience is not required—we provide onboarding and support to build the necessary domain expertise. 
You do not need to meet every requirement to apply. 
If you have strong experience in similar technical environments, a passion for safety, and operations, we encourage you to apply. 

Candidate Profile 
•    The ideal candidate demonstrates a strong safety mindset, sound technical judgment, and the ability to operate effectively in a structured, procedure-driven environment. 
•    Microsoft encourages applications from candidates with diverse technical backgrounds who are motivated to learn and contribute to a high-performing datacenter operations team. 
Security Requirements 
Candidates must successfully complete the Microsoft Cloud Background Check upon hire and maintain ongoing compliance throughout employment.

jobs.occupation: Executive Assistant to the Secretary General (maternity cover)
jobs.description:
Are you a strategic thinker, structured and with exceptional execution and communication skills? And do you have experience with executive and strategic support to senior management and knowledge of humanitarian and global affairs? We are looking for an experienced, proactive, extrovert and solutions oriented Executive Assistant to the Secretary General of the Danish Refugee Council (DRC). You will support the Secretary General in her daily work, work closely with the DRC Executive Management Team and engage with a variety of internal and external stakeholders.

About the job

The office of the Secretary General is a small dynamic team, supporting the Secretary General, the Executive Management Team, the Board of Directors, and the Council of DRC. The office also supports DRC’s overall organisational processes and its overall strategy, provides management and administrative support to the Secretary General, and organises global staff meetings. The office works and coordinates closely with departments in headquarters as well as DRC offices across the world.

 

Your key responsibilities will include:

·         Day-to-day comprehensive executive support and advice to the Secretary General, including on external engagements, positioning and communication, in close coordination with relevant teams. Liaising and communicating clearly and professionally on behalf of the Secretary General internally in DRC and with external stakeholders.

·         Support to the Executive Management Team (EMT), including preparation of agendas and presentations, decision-making documents and minutes, follow-up to decisions, and preparation of regular bilateral meetings between the SG and EMT members, including agenda setting. 

·         Coordinating and advising on processes for preparing the Secretary General’s external engagements, including drafting and proof reading of products (briefs, talking points, presentations etc.) for the Secretary General, and ensure timely and efficient follow-ups and minutes, and feedback to relevant teams.

·         Making sure that the Secretary General receives information requiring her attention and action and managing the Secretary General’s calendar.

·         Identify opportunities to simplify processes and strengthen ways of working through digital tools, automation and AI-enabled solutions.

·         Ensuring expense management in Microsoft Dynamics, related to SG travels, events and meetings (primary task of student assistant).

·         Ensuring legalisation of documents required across the organisation, including notarisation, apostilles, and coordination with embassies and translation services (primary task of student assistant).

 

About you

To be successful in this role we expect you to have:

·         A relevant master’s degree in international relations, political science or similar.

·         Excellent collaboration, analytical, organisational and communication skills, a flexible and solution-oriented attitude, and a structured and independent way of working with the ability to see the bigger picture while maintaining a strong attention to detail and high-quality deliverables.

·         Ability to maintain overview of a broad operational and political portfolio, advise on priorities and ensure timely execution and follow-up.

·         Solid knowledge of humanitarian affairs and operations, as well as international relations and developments impacting the work of DRC.

·         Experience in interacting with many different stakeholders, including high level, ideally from diplomacy and/or external relations from a global organisation.

·         Ability to deliver high-quality analytical inputs, and to draft complex briefing materials, talking points, and political or legal reports in fast-paced, high-pressure environment is required.

·         Full professional proficiency in Danish and English. Basic knowledge of French and/or Spanish is desirable.

 

All employees should master DRC's core competencies:

Striving for excellence: You focus on reaching results while ensuring an efficient process. 

Collaborating: You involve relevant parties and encourage feedback. 

Taking the lead: You take ownership and initiative while aiming for innovation. 

Communicating: You listen and speak effectively and honestly. 

Demonstrating integrity: You uphold and promote the highest standards of ethical and professional conduct in relation to our values and Code of Conduct, including safeguarding against sexual exploitation, abuse and harassment.

We offer

An interesting workplace with excellent colleagues and plenty of scope for contribution with your own ideas. The possibility of working closely with and supporting the Secretary General and the Executive Management Team, as well as colleagues across our global organisation.

Contract length: 9 months with the possibility of extension (maternity cover)

Work location: Lyngbyvej 100, 2100 Copenhagen Ø, just by Ryparken station

Start date: mid-November 2026 or the soonest hereafter

Salary and conditions will be in accordance with the agreement between DRC and AC. This is a national position for which local terms and conditions apply. Salary will be determined based on qualifications.

Please note that you need to have the right to work in Denmark (through nationality or existing work visa) in order to be considered for this role. 

 

Application process

All applicants must upload a cover letter and an updated CV in English (no longer than four pages) as well as degree certificate. Applications sent by email will not be considered.

Closing date for applications: 2 September 2026. We expect to conduct interviews in September. 

Further information 

For questions regarding the vacancy please contact Vibeke Bach Madsen, Corporate Strategic Advisor in the Secretary General’s Office: vibeke.bach.madsen@drc.ngo. We will do our best to respond to as many inquiries as possible.

For more information about the Danish Refugee Council, please visit our website drc.ngo.

Danish Refugee Council is an equal opportunity employer. We are committed to creating an inclusive and positive work environment based on mutual respect for all employees. All applicants are considered for employment regardless of personal characteristics or attributes.

jobs.occupation: Junior Planner
jobs.description:
Are you curious about how bestselling fashion products stay available in stores and online around the world? Do you enjoy working with data and finding solutions? If you're looking for a place where you can learn, grow and make an impact from day one, this could be your next step.

Join SELECTED's Essentials department as our new Junior Planner and become part of the team behind one of our most important business areas. Together, we ensure that our bestselling products are available when and where our customers need them, across international markets.

YOUR TEAM
Essentials is home to SELECTED's Never Out Of Stock programme, also known as NOOS. Here, we work to keep our bestselling products available throughout the year by balancing customer demand, inventory and product availability. To make that happen, we work closely with colleagues across Sales, Buying and Product, as well as with our international suppliers. 
You'll join a skilled and supportive team where knowledge is shared openly, responsibility comes early and you'll have plenty of opportunities to learn, develop and make an impact.

YOUR ROLE
As a Junior Planner, you'll help ensure that SELECTED's bestselling products are available throughout the year. By combining data, analysis and close collaboration with colleagues across the business, you'll see how every planning decision helps keep our bestselling products moving.
From day one, you'll contribute to the team's work while developing your analytical skills and commercial understanding. As you grow in the role, you'll gradually take on more responsibility and build your expertise within different planning disciplines. Depending on your development and business needs, you'll have the opportunity to specialise within areas such as demand planning or replenishment planning.

Your tasks will include:

• 
Monitoring sales, stock levels and product availability across international markets

• 
Analysing data and identifying trends that support planning and business decisions

• 
Supporting forecasting, replenishment and purchasing activities

• 
Preparing reports and maintaining planning data in our systems

• 
Collaborating with colleagues across Sales, Buying and Product to ensure an efficient product flow

• 
Contributing ideas that help improve planning processes and commercial performance.

YOUR PROFILE
We believe you'll thrive if you're curious about how a business works, enjoy analysing data and are motivated by turning data into meaningful business decisions. You're eager to learn, enjoy collaborating across teams and are ready to take responsibility while making a real contribution to the business. In addition, we imagine that you:

• 
Hold a relevant degree within Supply Chain Management, Business, Economics, Engineering or a similar analytical field

• 
Have experience working with Microsoft Excel and are eager to strengthen your analytical toolbox

• 
Work in a structured and detail-oriented way

• 
Communicate confidently in English, both written and spoken.

WE LOOK FORWARD TO HEARING FROM YOU
If you have any questions about the position, please contact Nidal Himidi on +45 52 15 12 83. Otherwise, please send your application and CV as soon as possible and no later than 7 September 2026. We review applications on an ongoing basis and reserve the right to remove the job advertisement, when we find the right candidate.  

LOCATION: Brande, Denmark.
